The paper introduces a novel representation of 2D airfoil shapes and 3D blade/wing designs called the separable shape tensor framework.
The key idea is to decouple affine deformations (scaling, rotation, shear) from higher-order undulations in the shape.
Discrete airfoil shapes are represented as elements of the Grassmannian G(n,2), where n is the number of landmarks defining the shape.
The Landmark-Affine (LA) standardization is used to map discrete shapes to the Grassmannian in a scale and translation invariant manner.
The separable representation enables independent control over different types of shape deformations, facilitating more flexible and interpretable aerodynamic design optimization.
The framework also enables consistent interpolation of 2D airfoil shapes into 3D blade/wing designs, reducing the parameter count compared to traditional approaches.
The authors note that the separable shape tensor representation is closely related to the concept of Kendall shape spaces developed in the 1970s.
The proposed approach is presented as an analytic generative model for airfoil shapes, in contrast to alternative AI-based generative models and nonlinear dimension reduction techniques.
The authors provide detailed computational routines for learning the manifold-valued generative model of shapes in seconds, based on the Grassmannian structure.
Key benefits of the approach include decoupling affine and higher-order deformations, representation independence, and consistent 3D blade/wing design.
The work aims to enable more flexible, interpretable, and computationally efficient aerodynamic design optimization compared to traditional methods.
The separable shape tensor framework is motivated by the need to study the impacts of manufacturing defects and damage on aerodynamic performance.
The authors highlight the importance of innovations in computational domains for the future of computational fluid dynamics research.
The proposed representation is intended to inform rotation- and reflection-invariant designs of 2D airfoil shapes and enable new interpretations of the shape space.
Implementations and examples of the separable shape tensor framework are available on GitHub (Doronina et al. 2022).
